title: Line-Skip Pass Prices
titleTail: : Magic Mountain update and dated park prices
h1: What a line-skip pass costs at every park on this site
description: Magic Mountain’s current Fast Lane Reserve/Ultimate terms and advertised starting price, plus other parks’ dated Fast Lane and Quick Queue examples.
summary: Magic Mountain’s October 9, 2026 update distinguishes Fast Lane Reserve and Fast Lane Ultimate from older price models. Other parks’ existing September 2026 price examples retain their stated dates and source limits. Check the live product for your actual visit.
ownership: This page records dated price evidence. Reservation mechanics, participating rides, admission and event exclusions, and buying considerations are explained in the line-skip guide.

rows.label: Fast Lane at Six Flags Over Texas, per person per day
rows.note: The one Six Flags park whose full 2026 date calendar was observable in September; it is the sample the other parks' bands are modeled on. Weekday floors sit near the bottom, Fright Fest Saturdays near the top.

rows.label: Fast Lane at Great Adventure (NJ) or Great America (IL), per person per day
rows.note: Both run the same dated Fast Lane model under the same parent. Great Adventure's haunt-season Saturdays are the strongest demand of the four Six Flags parks on this site; Great America's band behaves the same at slightly softer peaks.

rows.label: Fast Lane at Knott's Berry Farm, per person per day
rows.note: One wristband, unlimited use on the covered ride list for the day. Knott's own Fast Lane page listed from $75 in September 2026 with observed March Saturdays around $129; Scary Farm nights price separately above this band.

rows.label: All Season Fast Lane add-on at Knott’s Berry Farm
rows.note: A season-long add-on to an associated season pass. Knott’s listed $999 in September 2026 with promotional pricing observed down to the mid-$600s. These historical Knott’s figures are not quotes for Magic Mountain’s current add-ons; compare the live price and participating-park terms with your own expected visits.

rows.label: Quick Queue Unlimited at SeaWorld Orlando, per person per day
rows.note: SeaWorld's own pricing guide listed Quick Queue Unlimited from $143.99 online against a $177.97 gate figure. A year-round Quick Queue product sat at $199 for pass-holders, which is the multi-visit version of the same arithmetic.

rows.label: Quick Queue at SeaWorld San Antonio, per person per day
rows.note: Priced by date through the purchase flow rather than published as a calendar, so this band is inferred from the Orlando and San Diego products rather than read off a page. Treat it as planning shape and check the date.

rows.label: Quick Queue Unlimited at SeaWorld San Diego, per person per day
rows.note: Sold standalone by date and inside the $139.99 Ultimate Bundle that also includes admission and the All-Day Dining Deal — the bundle is usually the better buy if you were taking both anyway.

sections.heading: Magic Mountain: a verified starting price, not an inferred range
body: As of October 9, 2026, Magic Mountain’s official page advertised Daily Fast Lane starting from $49, plus applicable fees and taxes. That starting figure is not a quote for October 15, does not identify an upper price bound and is not assigned here to Reserve or Ultimate. The former $45–$170 Magic Mountain band inferred from another park has been removed.

Magic Mountain names two all-day products: Fast Lane Reserve and Fast Lane Ultimate. Reserve holds a virtual place and provides a return time; Ultimate generates immediate Fast Lane entry, not immediate boarding. Both allow one reservation at a time, with riding completed before checking in for the next ready reservation.

Park admission and Fright Fest Haunted Attractions are not included. Products are per guest, cannot be shared, have limited daily sales and selected-date validity, require a mobile browser with internet, and cover participating attractions subject to change. Check the live purchase flow and current participating rides before buying.

Sources checked October 9, 2026: [Magic Mountain Fast Lane and FAQs](https://www.sixflags.com/magicmountain/fast-lane) and [Six Flags Fast Lane program updates](https://www.sixflags.com/blog/fast-lane-updates). Older THE FLASH Pass advice is historical; a generic three-tier model does not describe Magic Mountain’s current pair of all-day products.

sections.heading: The Legolands: the honest nothing-to-buy answer
body: Neither US Legoland sells a comparable line-skip product. There is no Fast Lane, no FLASH successor, no Quick Queue equivalent at Carlsbad or Winter Haven — the answer to 'what does line-skip cost at Legoland' is that there is nothing to buy.

This is not an oversight to work around but a fact to plan around: the Legoland ride roster is built for the under-tens and their adults, queue throughput is gentler than at the coaster parks, and the money that would have gone to line-skip goes further on the second-day ticket that Legoland's own pricing practically gives away.

howToSave: Check the actual visit’s operating hours, ride availability, queues and exact-date quote before buying. A weekday may be quieter, but it does not establish that a pass is unnecessary.
Compare the final checkout price, fees and terms for the product you want. No universal online-versus-gate discount is verified for Magic Mountain’s current Reserve and Ultimate products.

Check the bundle before the standalone product at SeaWorld. San Diego's Ultimate Bundle wrapped admission, All-Day Dining, and Quick Queue Unlimited into $139.99 in September 2026 — less than the Orlando standalone top of band alone.

For a season add-on, compare its current quoted price with your own expected visits and check the associated admission pass and participating-park terms; there is no universal six-visit break-even point.
Check live sale availability before deciding when to purchase. Magic Mountain limits daily sales; neither availability at the gate nor a cheaper morning-of-visit price is guaranteed.

faqs.q: Can one line-skip pass cover two different companies' parks?
faqs.a: A single-day product is park- and date-specific. Season-pass and membership benefits have separate participating-park rules linked to the associated admission pass. Check the exact entitlement; shared Fast Lane branding does not establish park admission or access to every park.

faqs.q: Is THE FLASH Pass still a thing?
faqs.a: Older THE FLASH Pass advice is historical at Magic Mountain. Its current official page names Fast Lane Reserve and Fast Lane Ultimate, and the Six Flags program update explains their reservation platform. Check the current park product rather than mapping old tiers onto it.

freshness.sourceNote: Magic Mountain product terms and Daily Fast Lane starting from $49 were retrieved from https://www.sixflags.com/magicmountain/fast-lane and corroborated for program mechanics by https://www.sixflags.com/blog/fast-lane-updates on October 9, 2026. This starting price is not a visit-date/tier quote or a price range; the previous modeled Magic Mountain row is removed. Other rows retain September 2026 observations and stated source limits: Knott’s from $75, Orlando Quick Queue Unlimited $143.99 online/$177.97 gate, San Diego $139.99 Ultimate Bundle, and Over Texas published calendar examples. Great Adventure/Great America and San Antonio rows remain planning estimates as their row notes explain; they are not new October verification.
